answer: The admission ceremony enforces identity uniqueness by requiring 900 units per AI agent. A verifier maps each submission to a global registry to block cloned IDs, ensuring an honest agent pays 900 units while 1,000 fakes incur a 900,000 unit cost to gain entry. Each agent provides a unique inlet for data, akin to a rhythmic pulse, which is cross-indexed at the ceremony dawn to detect duplication. Any evidence collision voids the identity and fees are locked for sixty days, assuming that pooling of compute cannot bypass this registry.
